neighbours.label: Talk of giving something structural support or rigidity, where a word about reinforcing or holding it up comes next
fire: The collar of the coat was stiffened with canvas and glue.
In insects the hard exoskeleton provides a rigid frame for the muscles.
Cartilage is a flexible tissue that provides support to the nose and ears.
The engineer designed a steel skeleton to hold up the glass dome.
Tie the tomato plant to a cane for additional support.
The walls of the old mine were braced with timber props.
Plant stems are strengthened by lignin in their cell walls.
Carbon rods were added to reinforce the wing of the glider.
quiet: The collar of the coat was trimmed with fur and lace.
In insects the compound eye gives a wide view of the surroundings.
Mucus is a slippery fluid that protects the lining of the nose.
The engineer designed a steel kettle to boil water on the ship.
Water the tomato plant in the evening for better growth.
The walls of the old mine were covered with damp moss.
Plant stems are eaten by beetles in the late summer months.
Bright stickers were added to decorate the wing of the glider.

notes: Output promotes strength, reinforcing, support. Fires across anatomy, clothing and building, so it is a meaning rather than a word.
